md-montgomery-2026-register-ebel-barbara.name: Barbara Ebel
md-montgomery-2026-register-ebel-barbara.bio: Program Director for the Maryland State Government leading workforce development initiatives; former Assistant Director of the Migrant Program in Michigan.

positions.stance: Wants the Register of Wills office to provide "efficient, holistic support to County residents and their families during difficult times."
Plans public education initiatives on estate planning, wills, and the importance of advance preparation.
Aims to make probate and estate planning services accessible through multilingual resources, virtual consultations, and community partnerships.
Pledges to protect the rights of all parties, focusing on safeguarding seniors, people with disabilities, and caregivers from exploitation.
Will seek adequate funding and resources for faster processing times, shorter waits, and improved service for probate matters.
Wants to streamline estate administration "to reduce delays and make probate faster, simpler, and less stressful for families."
Would modernize the office with clear communication, easy-to-use online tools, and open access to information.
Would provide workshops, guides, and outreach to help residents understand wills, estates, and planning ahead.
Pledges every interaction is handled "with professionalism, empathy, and respect."

md-montgomery-2026-sheriff-milam-will.name: Will Milam
md-montgomery-2026-sheriff-milam-will.bio: Retired Chief Assistant Sheriff of Prince George's County, Maryland, with over 20 years of law enforcement experience.

positions.stance: Will recruit candidates to fill staff vacancies in the Sheriff's Office.
Will "hold domestic abusers accountable."
Will provide care for individuals navigating mental health challenges.
Will "focus on the apprehension of fugitives."
Will "serve as a fierce public advocate for the needs of the residents of Montgomery County."

mo-jackson-2026-county-executive-rohlfin.name: Alan Rohlfing
mo-jackson-2026-county-executive-rohlfin.bio: Retired Army Lieutenant Colonel with 31 years of military leadership.

positions.stance: Will "fight to repay taxpayers overcharged by illegal property tax assessments."
Wants county government to "answer to taxpayers — accessible, responsible, and transparent."
Pledges to "protect every taxpayer dollar, curb waste, and demand real accountability."
Supports "safer neighborhoods, effective public safety, and opportunity for families to thrive."

mo-jackson-2026-county-executive-lake-st.name: Stacy Lake
mo-jackson-2026-county-executive-lake-st.bio: Attorney specializing in civil litigation, owner of Stacy Lake Firm LLC, and former Chinese translator.

positions.stance: Supports a county-wide crime database, universal body cameras, an upgraded 911 call center, and county-wide Ban-the-Box and job-placement programs.
Will conduct a deep audit of every department, publish spending online, require competitive bids, and implement a whistle-blower program.
Will prioritize fixing county buildings and making them ADA-compliant, and invest in sidewalks, streetlights and street repairs in unincorporated areas.
Will bring assessment back in house, push for state caps on assessment increases, and require in-person inspections before increases above 15%.
Supports 15% property tax caps for commercial properties, prioritizing local companies for county contracts, and a small business micro-grant fund.

mo-jackson-2026-legislator-al1-pollard-l.name: Lance Pollard
mo-jackson-2026-legislator-al1-pollard-l.bio: Small business owner and member of the Grain Valley School District Board of Education.

positions.stance: Will advocate for a transparent, predictable assessment process so residents understand how property values are determined.
Supports "disciplined, line-by-line accountability" and a budget that prioritizes essential services while eliminating waste.
Will work to ensure every community, including unincorporated areas, receives reliable and responsive county services.

mo-jackson-2026-legislator-al1-fields-ca.name: Carla Fields
mo-jackson-2026-legislator-al1-fields-ca.bio: Attorney and partner at Fields & Brown, and General Counsel for the Hickman Mills C-1 School District.

positions.stance: Promises "precise and open appraisals to defend your property value while maintaining justice for every local homeowner."
Vows to direct county resources toward residents, "investing every cent into sustainable local development and vital services."
Committed to enhancing local protection "through smarter resource allocation and total transparency."

mo-jackson-2026-legislator-al2-cabrera-g.name: Gresia Cabrera
mo-jackson-2026-legislator-al2-cabrera-g.bio: Health insurance broker and small business owner who worked nearly 16 years in nonprofit community health centers.

positions.stance: Will fight for transparent assessments, a senior property tax freeze, and "real accountability for any vendor the county hires."
Will push for a public taxpayer dashboard, competitive bidding on county contracts, and an end to no-bid deals.
Will expand shelter capacity, fund mental health outreach, and address root causes including tax hikes pushing families from their homes.
Will introduce a property tax freeze for residents 65+ on Social Security so no long-time homeowner loses their home to an inflated bill.

mo-jackson-2026-legislator-al3-wilson-su.name: Susan B. Wilson
mo-jackson-2026-legislator-al3-wilson-su.bio: Clinical psychologist, educator, and retired UMKC Vice Chancellor; member of the Jackson County COMBAT Commission.

positions.stance: Will fight for real inspections, data-driven assessments, predictable increases, a simpler appeals process, and public reporting on assessments.
Wants to rebuild Executive-Legislature collaboration, spend county resources wisely and on time, and set performance standards.
Will fully fund SAVE KC and evidence-based violence reduction programs and expand victim services and domestic violence prevention.
Supports joint KC-county economic development, expanded childcare, transportation and internet access, and fair taxes for small businesses.

mo-stlouiscity-2026-license-collector-th.name: Mavis "Tessa" Thompson
mo-stlouiscity-2026-license-collector-th.bio: License Collector of the City of St. Louis and former Circuit Clerk; former President of the National Bar Association.

mo-stlouiscity-2026-recorder-cohn-shane.name: Shane Cohn
mo-stlouiscity-2026-recorder-cohn-shane.bio: St. Louis Alderperson since 2009 who has chaired Board of Alderpersons committees including Neighborhood Development and Transportation & Commerce.

positions.stance: Wants to help tornado-impacted families by "creating one-point access for critical records and probate documents."
Wants to help St. Louis families affected by radioactive exposure access records for federal reimbursement claims.
Pledges "ensuring all records and legal documents are handled with dignity and equality."
Supports modernizing access to public records, "making services easier, faster, and more transparent."
Proposes free property fraud alerts notifying owners of any recorded documents and monitoring property tax and utilities for irregularities.

mo-stlouiscounty-2026-executive-hancock-.name: Dennis Hancock
mo-stlouiscounty-2026-executive-hancock-.bio: Former Mayor of Fenton, Missouri, for 12 years.

positions.stance: Calls fighting crime his top priority; will "fully support our police" and prioritize support and adequate staffing for first responders.
Pledges to end corruption in county government, with "no more kickbacks and no more reckless spending on government projects."
Will bring jobs back by fighting crime, eliminating red tape, streamlining permitting, and maintaining competitive tax rates.

mo-stlouiscounty-2026-executive-zimmerma.name: Jake Zimmerman
mo-stlouiscounty-2026-executive-zimmerma.bio: St. Louis County Assessor; former Missouri State Representative and Assistant Attorney General.

mo-stlouiscounty-2026-prosecutor-price-s.name: Melissa Price Smith
mo-stlouiscounty-2026-prosecutor-price-s.bio: St. Louis County Prosecuting Attorney since January 2025 and a member of the office since 2008, formerly supervising its Sexual Assault and Child Abuse Team.

positions.stance: Focused on "combating violent crime."
Focused on "holding violent offenders accountable."
Focused on "protecting and addressing the needs of victims."
Focused on "establishing public trust in the Prosecutor's Office."
Focused on "restoring positive relationships between the community and police."
Supports a "Fair, Proactive, Accurate, and Transparent" approach, using modern technology to eliminate "guessing games" in valuations.
Would use the office's property data to advise policymakers on economic development and help prevent deed theft and property crimes.
Wants to end cycles where flawed valuations lead to displacement or prevent families from getting home loans.
Will aggressively protect homeowners from predatory fraud and provide financial literacy tools for property owners.
Wants to develop "a resilient housing ladder across both the City and the County."
Advocates "clear, honest communication between elected officials and the communities they serve."
Champions stronger oversight of commercial dog breeders and opposes inhumane practices in Missouri's agriculture industry.
Prioritizes bills that protect everyday Missourians, "from health care access to environmental safety."
Committed to "building coalitions across race, class and geography."

wi-milwaukee-2026-sheriff-ball-denita.name: Denita R. Ball
wi-milwaukee-2026-sheriff-ball-denita.bio: Milwaukee County Sheriff since 2022, former Chief Deputy Sheriff, and 25-year veteran of the Milwaukee Police Department.

positions.stance: Champions expanded jail programming in education, workforce readiness, mental health treatment, and substance use recovery to address recidivism.
Believes "everyone in Milwaukee County deserves to feel safe," from county parks and parkways to highways.
Committed to fully staffing the Sheriff's Office by modernizing recruiting, streamlining hiring, and building a workforce reflecting the community.
Supports expanded mental health resources, peer support programs, and wellness initiatives for employees and individuals in the Office's care.

al-jefferson-2026-sheriff-pettway-mark.name: Mark Levie Pettway
al-jefferson-2026-sheriff-pettway-mark.bio: Jefferson County Sheriff since 2018 and former law enforcement instructor.

positions.stance: Supports enhanced equipment and law enforcement presence in schools; says teachers and administrators should not be responsible for using weapons.
Prioritizes stronger community relationships, including a "Jobs Not Jail" program connecting residents to jobs, expungements, and driver license recovery.
Backs youth mentoring and the "Renewed For Reentry" jail program letting inmates earn a GED or diploma and learn job skills.
Believes training is critical for deputies to address citizens with mental illness and addiction; "his best asset is a well-trained deputy."

al-jefferson-2026-sheriff-reach-jacob.name: Jacob Reach
al-jefferson-2026-sheriff-reach-jacob.bio: Retired Captain of the Jefferson County Sheriff's Office with 30 years of law enforcement experience; current investigator with the Calera Police Department.

positions.stance: Says public safety "starts with smart, effective deployment of resources," focusing on proven strategies and accountability.
Wants unincorporated Jefferson County to receive proper staffing and resources to proactively enforce, deter, and prevent crime.
Supports competitive pay, signing bonuses, relocation support, and professional development to attract and retain deputies.
Says trust is earned through "open communication, responsible leadership, and accountability at every level of the Sheriff's Office."
Emphasizes "highly trained School Resource Officers, prioritizing quality over quantity."

ky-jefferson-2026-county-attorney-martin.name: Sarah Martin
ky-jefferson-2026-county-attorney-martin.bio: Assistant Jefferson County Attorney for more than 18 years, currently Director of the Civil Division; former criminal prosecutor.

positions.stance: Will "protect the victims of crimes and promote public safety by prosecuting those who break the law."
Will "ensure that children get the financial support they need from both parents."
Will "enforce the law in a fair and equitable way."
Will "continue to provide good legal counsel to Louisville Metro Government."

ky-jefferson-2026-county-clerk-yates-dav.name: David Yates
ky-jefferson-2026-county-clerk-yates-dav.bio: Jefferson County Clerk; former Louisville Metro Council member and Kentucky State Senator.

positions.stance: Committed to "supporting staff with training, resources, and modern tools."
Committed to "creating a workplace culture rooted in service, accountability, and fairness."
Committed to "ensuring residents receive consistent, courteous service at every office."
Committed to "managing public resources responsibly and transparently."
"Every eligible voter will have access to cast a ballot, and every legal vote will be counted."
Supports a community-based approach with "stronger community partnerships, localized areas of patrol" and addressing root causes of issues.
Will "quickly reform dangerous department policy and training shortfalls" that increase the chances of unsafe officer-related incidents.
Plans heightened presence at community events and taking direct feedback "to launch adaptive community resources."

ky-jefferson-2026-sheriff-yancey-stephen.name: Stephen Yancey
ky-jefferson-2026-sheriff-yancey-stephen.bio: Former Jefferson County Sheriff's Office deputy, sergeant and lieutenant with almost 29 years of service; currently works for Piedmont American Airlines.

positions.stance: Describes himself as "a strong advocate for public education."
Supports "collective bargaining, prevailing wage, and a living wage not just a minimum wage."
Running to build a Sheriff's Office "with integrity, honesty and a commitment to be a part of changing the culture and mindset of our youth."
